about.title: Norco Slip & Fall & Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Norco's mix of equestrian trails, local shops along Hamner Avenue, and businesses near the I-15 corridor means residents and visitors are constantly moving between properties owned by different people and companies. When a wet floor, broken step, uneven pavement, or poor lighting causes a fall, the property owner or manager may be liable — but only if it can be shown they knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn visitors. That's why acting quickly matters: photographing the hazard, getting witness names, and requesting that any surveillance footage be preserved before it's erased can make a real difference. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves, but we connect Norco residents hurt in falls with an independent attorney who can evaluate the circumstances of the property, the hazard, and what the owner knew, all without any upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a California Premises Liability Claim

items.title: Proving Notice Takes Timing
items.desc: California law requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can move quickly to request maintenance logs, incident reports, and inspection records before they're routinely discarded.

items.title: Surveillance Video Doesn't Last
items.desc: Many Norco businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks. A formal preservation request sent early can be the difference between having video evidence and having none.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Recovery
items.desc: Even if a property owner argues you weren't watching where you were walking, California's pure comparative fault rule means you may still recover a portion of damages based on the share of fault attributed to the property owner.

items.question: I fell at a business near Hamner Avenue — do I need proof the owner knew about the hazard?
items.answer: Generally, yes. California premises liability law typically requires showing the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the dangerous condition and failed to address it. That's why documenting the hazard with photos and identifying any witnesses right after the fall is so important. An attorney can help determine whether that notice requirement is met in your situation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Norco?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit, though claims against a public entity, such as a city-owned property, involve a much shorter deadline. Missing these windows can bar your claim entirely, so it's worth having an attorney review the timeline early.

items.question: What if I was partly distracted or not looking where I was walking when I fell?
items.answer: Being partially at fault doesn't automatically prevent you from recovering compensation. California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning your recovery may simply be reduced by your percentage of responsibility rather than eliminated. An independent attorney can help assess how fault might be allocated in your specific case.
